Your Favorite 90s Video Game Is Your Biggest Personality Red Flag

post // May 26, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

Your favorite '90s game might be your red flag. Be honest:

  • Super Mario 64 avoids structure.
  • Zelda turns pain into lore.
  • Sonic 2 rushes everything.
  • NiGHTS lives in delusion.
  • Street Fighter II argues to win.
  • Pokémon keeps backup options.
  • Resident Evil fears losing control.

Here's the breakdown.

Super Mario 64: avoids structure

Mario 64 (1996) was the first great 3D playground. You could chase Power Stars in almost any order, skip whole chunks of the castle and just run around the courtyard doing backflips. Mario 64 people see a to-do list and go explore the castle instead.

Zelda: turns pain into lore

Zelda fans don't have trauma. They have a timeline. Every sad moment, every ruined kingdom and every "what happened here?" becomes a theory. Whether you grew up on A Link to the Past or Ocarina of Time, you know somebody who can explain the timeline split better than their own feelings.

Sonic 2: rushes everything

Gotta go fast. Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (1992) was built for speed, and Sonic 2 people bring that energy everywhere: skipping instructions, skimming texts and speedrunning conversations. Spin dash first, ask questions later.

NiGHTS into Dreams: lives in delusion

NiGHTS (1996) literally takes place inside dreams, and NiGHTS fans have been living there ever since. Flying through dreamscapes on the Sega Saturn? Beautiful. Still waiting on a proper modern sequel? That's the delusion.

Street Fighter II: argues to win

If you played Street Fighter II (1991), you've argued about cheap moves, button mashing and whether a round "counts." Street Fighter II people don't lose. They get robbed.

Pokémon: keeps backup options

Six in the party and a PC full of boxes. Pokémon Red and Blue taught a whole generation to always keep options in storage, just in case. Pokémon people never fully close a door.

Resident Evil: fears losing control

Limited ammo. Limited saves. Tank controls and a door-opening animation that makes you hold your breath. Resident Evil (1996) trained people to hoard every herb and never waste a single bullet. Resident Evil people need to know exactly what's in the inventory at all times.

Quick answers

What year did Super Mario 64 come out? 1996, on the Nintendo 64.

What is NiGHTS into Dreams? A 1996 Sega Saturn game from Sonic Team where you fly through dream worlds as NiGHTS.

When did Street Fighter II come out? In arcades in 1991.

When did the first Resident Evil come out? In 1996, on the PlayStation.

Your turn

Which game hits too close to home? Drop your favorite '90s game in the comments for Part 2.
